passage.quote:
Model-assisted formalization delegates instruction definitions and proof
candidates to smaller models using shared, reviewed semantic foundations.
Each task supplies the source passages, fixed interfaces and acceptance obligations
for a bounded instruction family. The coordinator develops those foundations,
maintains coverage, and evaluates the generation and review workflow; routine
instruction-by-instruction expansion belongs to the delegated workers.
Lean checks submitted proofs, while source review and
independent checks address whether their definitions describe the intended
behavior. Generation records identify the inputs, outputs, checking results,
and costs needed to assess reproducibility and cost effectiveness. A generator
agreeing with its own definitions does not establish semantic fidelity.

summary: Delegate bounded instruction families to smaller models against fixed semantic foundations and source-derived obligations.
Accept generated definitions only after mechanical proof checks and separate semantic review, preserving all missing and unresolved coverage.
Keep delegated low-cost semantic review independent of generation and evaluate its ability to detect incorrect definitions.
Evaluate the frozen workflow on held-out tasks with complete attempt, cost and reviewer-effort records.
Validate checking code before dispatch and distinguish checker repairs from worker failures.
Distinguish worker-derived computation definitions from coordinator-supplied bodies, and account separately for independent check preparation.
remaining: The source-section inventory, recorded fresh/resumed Luna calls, pinned worker provisioning and replay, selected-form provenance and targeted semantic mutation probes are implemented. Reviewed tasks cover selected integer, bitwise and binary32 forms with coordinator-supplied contracts. A three-family batch uses preflighted frozen checkers and preserves first-attempt outcomes separately from earlier repaired trials. A worker-derived computation pilot retains both accepted and unfinished proof packages under universal source-derived bit laws, with explicit proof guidance and coordinator preflight effort. An assisted continuation supplies reusable value lemmas and preserves original failed attempts separately from later acceptance; generalization remains unmeasured. A separate fixed-context OpenRouter reviewer route and blinded development cases are implemented. Reliable reviewer-quality evidence, full form coverage, broader capability evidence, held-out evaluation and cost effectiveness remain unfinished.

from.quote:
Exploratory evaluation asks which tasks workers can complete and what assistance
they need; prompts and feedback may change while those attempts remain recorded.
A later productivity evaluation asks how much accepted work a fixed workflow
produces for the effort spent. It separates tasks used to improve prompts from
held-out tasks reserved for measuring the frozen workflow. Closely related forms are grouped to avoid
treating near-duplicates as independent evidence. Reports include every assigned
task, failed and interrupted attempts, repairs and reviewer interventions. They
separate first-attempt proof checking, eventual acceptance, semantic rejection
and unresolved cases, and do not generalize a narrow sample to the full ISA.

passage.quote:
This is **one adaptive development task**, not a held-out benchmark. It supports
the conclusion that the requested Luna configuration can finish this task after
feedback. It does not establish a full-ISA success rate or cost effectiveness.
